skill.name: prisma-next-quickstart
skill.description: Guides first-touch, greenfield, and existing-database adoption of Prisma Next through setup, connection, contract inference, and a verified first query.
skill.summary: Build a working Prisma Next connection and complete the first write-read cycle.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documentation links, and ordinary Prisma environment configuration. Confirmed risks are direct .env inspection, passing DATABASE_URL through command arguments, and default CLI telemetry.

remediation.issue: The workflow tells agents to read .env while checking DATABASE_URL.
remediation.suggestion: Check only whether DATABASE_URL exists and redact its value. Request permission before reading any environment file.

remediation.issue: Brownfield commands pass DATABASE_URL as a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a CLI mode that reads DATABASE_URL directly from the environment or secure input. Avoid placing expanded credentials in process arguments.

remediation.issue: Agent-invoked Prisma Next commands send telemetry by default.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before telemetry-enabled runs or set DO_NOT_TRACK=1 for automated workflows. Explain how users can restore their preferred setting.

content.user_title: Start Prisma Next with a Working Database
content.value_statement: New and existing projects need a clear path to their first Prisma Next query. This skill guides setup, connection, contract inference, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Identifies first-touch, greenfield, and existing-database adoption paths.
Guides Prisma Next initialization for PostgreSQL or MongoDB projects.
Reviews configuration, contract, runtime, and environment prerequisites.
Guides a first database write and read against an existing model.
Explains contract inference, emission, signing, and database verification.
limitations: Does not migrate application code from another ORM.
Does not provide advanced queries, transactions, or raw SQL guidance.
Does not replace production migration planning and review.
Requires a reachable PostgreSQL or MongoDB database for verification.

use_cases.title: Orient a Scaffolded Project
use_cases.description: Review an existing Prisma Next scaffold and complete its first database round trip.
use_cases.target_user: Developers opening a generated or cloned project

use_cases.title: Create a New Project
use_cases.description: Initialize Prisma Next, configure the database, and verify the starter contract.
use_cases.target_user: Developers starting a PostgreSQL or MongoDB application

use_cases.title: Adopt an Existing Database
use_cases.description: Infer a contract from a live schema, review it, and sign the database marker.
use_cases.target_user: Teams adding Prisma Next to an established database

prompt_templates.title: Find My First Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Prisma Next project and identify my adoption path. Explain the contract location, then guide my first database round trip.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner orientation in an existing project

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a Greenfield Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Prisma Next in this project for [postgres or mongodb] using [psl or typescript]. Preserve existing files and verify the starter model.

prompt_templates.title: Adopt a Live Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide Prisma Next adoption for my existing [database type] database. Infer the contract, pause for review, then emit, sign, and verify it.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an Incomplete Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Prisma Next setup for contract paths, generated artifacts, runtime wiring, environment presence, marker status, and drift. Propose the smallest corrective sequence.

output_examples.input: I cloned a Prisma Next project. What should I do first?
output_examples.output: The project uses the PostgreSQL target and a PSL contract under the Prisma source directory. Next, verify the connection and round-trip one existing model.

output_examples.input: Help me use Prisma Next with an existing database.
output_examples.output: The brownfield path will infer a draft contract from the live schema. Review model names and constraints before emitting, signing, and verifying it.

output_examples.input: Initialization worked, but my first query fails.
output: Confirm the database variable exists without displaying its value.
Verify the configured contract path and emitted artifacts.
Check marker status and database drift before changing the contract.

best_practices: Read the project configuration and contract before proposing commands.
Complete one write-read cycle before expanding the data model.
Review inferred contracts before signing an existing database.
anti_patterns: Do not expose environment values while checking database configuration.
Do not edit generated contract artifacts by hand.
Do not use development schema synchronization for production releases.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers PostgreSQL and MongoDB targets supported by Prisma Next.

faq.question: Can it start a new project?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides initialization in the current project directory and verifies the starter contract.

faq.question: Can it adopt an existing database?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides contract inference, review, emission, marker signing, and drift verification.

faq.question: Does it migrate from another ORM?
faq.answer: No. Use a dedicated migration skill or treat the database as an existing schema.

faq.question: Will it design my complete data model?
faq.answer: No. It prioritizes a verified first query before broader contract design.

faq.question: Does Prisma Next collect telemetry?
faq.answer: The documented CLI enables anonymous telemetry by default. Users can disable it with supported environment variables or the telemetry command.
